title: Advancements in stress-testing methodologies for financial stability applications
summary: This ECB Occasional Paper (No 348) provides a comprehensive overview of stress-testing methodologies developed by the ECB's Working Group on Stress Testing (WGST) from 2018-2022. The paper covers 16 new stress-testing models including top-down credit risk, market risk, and profitability models; macro-micro models examining macroprudential policy interactions; and system-wide models capturing interconnectedness between banks and non-bank financial institutions.
key_points: The WGST developed 16 new stress-testing models between 2018-2022, with 11 covering areas not previously addressed by ECB's top-down toolkit
Five models replaced earlier versions in the STAMP€ tool; an additional five existing models were improved and two were referred for testing
13 new datasets were integrated, including transaction-level data, supporting model development
System-wide models (e.g., the ISA model) capture interconnectedness and contagion risks between banks and non-banking financial institutions
Top-down models focus on credit risk (IFRS 9 and regulatory parameters), market risk, and profitability analysis
Validation efforts combine ex ante and ex post elements, comparing model performance against banks' forecasts and back-testing against past exercises
why_it_matters: This paper documents ECB's internal stress-testing infrastructure for assessing bank solvency and financial stability. While not a direct market catalyst, it provides transparency into the analytical tools regulators use to evaluate systemic risks and conduct EU-wide stress tests that inform supervisory decisions and macroprudential policy.
macro_context: The paper discusses how stress-testing methodologies support macroprudential policy evaluation and financial stability assessment. Macro-micro models examine interactions between macroprudential policies, monetary policy changes, and financial stability outcomes.
market_structure_context: This source focuses on bank-level stress testing and regulatory frameworks rather than market structure topics such as trading venue operations, liquidity provision, order flow dynamics, or market participant behavior.
